findings.title: Generated CRUD and supported public read can disclose server secret bytes
findings.witness: Minimal configured model M has writable label and token server=random_secret; admitted M.create {label:"x"} yields result.data.token=64hex because result is full changed row. A supported public read mark grants all declared fields and secretFields=[], so later M.read can return that same string; no secret-kind detector recognizes primitive hex. Mutation with no readable-field grant also returns ordinary hidden data. HTTP serializes the MutationResult object as outcome.result; raw changed-row data appears under JSON result.data.token, not an additional read projection.
findings.prerequisites: Compatible generated descriptors/real producers + registered model + admitted caller + assembly interfaces factory on HTTP route. Public-read arm separately requires supported public policy mark; t18 fixture itself uses members and ruled-read refusal, not public serving.
findings.actual_consumer: state generatedCrudExecute -> canonical invoke -> assembly buildInvoker -> HTTP JSON serialization; public slice -> query projection. No deployed/compiler/runtime proof.
findings.strongest_counterevidence: Caller cannot supply token; conflicts exclude serverOnly; generic viewer cleanCopy removes secret-kind values and explicit secretFields. Those controls do not cover plain hex secret with empty metadata or full successful row. T18 test sources deliberately assert raw row/hex as private engine results, not public privacy acceptance.
findings.required_fix_acceptance: Enforce never-readable secret using owning schema/value metadata at every changed-row/read/replay/serialization path; successful mutation returns receipt plus currently authorized changed-record projection. Preserve raw private engine row where legitimately needed and saved idempotency without exposing it. Add source-qualified first success/public-read/replay negative witnesses including no read policy and explicit secret grant refusal.
findings.uncertainty: Required confidentiality outcome already accepted; exact opaque storage representation/result transition needs owner-compatible migration, not chosen here.

findings.title: Streaming body bytes do not bound recursive pre-authorization hash work
findings.witness: Valid JSON below1MiB: {inputs:{record:{id:"r",version:"1",extra:[[[...null...]]]}}}; N nested arrays in tolerated ref extra member. Framing checks only declared top-level names; checkBoundRef checks id/version but no extra traversal; stableStringify recursively walks extra before by/shape/ref load. For sufficiently deep N it can exhaust call stack; exact threshold not executed.
findings.prerequisites: Authenticated HTTP session+valid CSRF/current UUID, compatible ref operation shape; permitted deep JSON parse in host. Alternate private canonical caller can supply same plain data.
findings.actual_consumer: HTTP handleOperationRequest -> checkBoundRef -> assembly canonical admit -> hashInputs. A caller forbidden by operation still causes hashing first.
findings.strongest_counterevidence: 1MiB cap, authentication/CSRF and closed top-level shape are real controls. JS executable getters/toJSON/cycles are not JSON transport inputs. Ref version1-15digit numeric conversion safe.
findings.required_fix_acceptance: Apply explicit depth/node/work admission at actual canonical input boundary before recursive hashing/allocation; iterative traversal can preserve digest/order. Retain tolerated ref extra-member semantics and exact raw hash bytes for admitted inputs; exceed budget loud before effects. Qualify finite adversarial-depth wire fixtures and bounded-resource refusal.
findings.uncertainty: Exact numeric cap/error/accepted-depth compatibility requires resource-contract owner; no new threshold selected. Stack threshold/source parse behavior unexecuted.

findings.title: Mixed-owner injected store has no enforced tenant row separation
findings.witness: Prerequisite shared store contains same model rows owned by teamsA/B. Caller active only inA admitted by members; policy grant members over fieldtitle no row-levelteam predicate. queryRecords scans both and evaluateBy uses callerA membership for every row; a ref toB id also loads bymodel+id. Checkpoint/receipt ownerA does not route or filter data.

Parent filters and cohort explicitowner comparison operate where supplied; receipt namespaces separated. No blanket deployed IDOR claim.

Preserve explicit public exceptions and authoritative same-owner mutation semantics; addA/B same-model read/ref denial witness against actual routing join.

findings.title: Query/recovery returned limit is not bounded scanning or memory
findings.witness: M containsN stored rows. Canonical M.read passes no limit; query engine requests every row, projects, filters and sorts; even limit1 elsewhere only rejects afterward. Recovery limit1 queries all claimed plus all uncertain rows, materializes and sorts; if claims fresh it may visit all before releasing any.
findings.prerequisites: Attacker can legitimately grow/read M or cause retained pending/uncertain work; host permits enough data. Recovery itself is private scheduler, not attacker-invocable endpoint proved.
findings.actual_consumer: Canonical generated read and nested readModel; D1 all(); work.dispatch.recover bound system driver.
findings.strongest_counterevidence: Complete-set semantics and nontruncate overflow are intentional. D1 quotas/Worker limits may abort, but no project-controlled scan/work bound established. Snapshot consistency/lifecycle old gaps not new here.
findings.required_fix_acceptance: Bound work/bytes/visited records at actual storage/driver join with indexed resumable pages and explicit budget refusal; preserve complete business query/all-or-reject behavior and recovery continuation. Push no caller limit as truncation. Include sparse stale claims, many denied rows and uncertain backlog witnesses.
findings.uncertainty: No specific row cap/query planner chosen; legitimate full queries may require explicit bounded-query contract. SQL query performance not measured.

Bound serialized member-row bytes and total work; avoid fixed cohort quota presented as semantics.

findings.title: Retry horizon cannot interrupt hung provider/evidence promises
findings.witness: Won committed claim, opts.callProvider returns a promise that never settles: drive awaits indefinitely and never records outcome. A stale-claim recovery may later release/re-drive while original provider call is still in flight. Callback lateness must remain uncertain, not definite failure.
findings.prerequisites: Private provider adapter lacks own bounded deadline/evidence/idempotency handling; no actual adapter deployed hang proved.
findings.actual_consumer: Cloudflare driveDispatchIntent awaits injected provider once; Work retry policy runs only after an outcome.
findings.strongest_counterevidence: Default eight attempts24h, held claim and stable outbox ID, uncertain classification on throws, caller can implement timeouts/idempotency. Scheduler being bounded does not time-bound this awaited port.
findings.required_fix_acceptance: Require actual provider/evidence port bounded lifetime and late-result/uncertainty correlation; cancellation must not claim physical nonacceptance. Qualify stale claim plus still-live original call and late settled response with actual provider idempotency before release/retry.
findings.uncertainty: Deadline/cancellation versus remote acceptance is owning effect policy; no automatic retry/cancel/ack choice selected. Pure Work/native kernel cannot supply it.

findings.title: SQL field metadata lookup admits inherited names as columns
findings.witness: Private query order/where field="constructor" or "toString": COLUMN_FIELDS[field] yields inherited function before regex and is returned as column; SQL interpolation emits function text, causing query error rather than data-column selection. Same code inD1 andDO.
findings.prerequisites: Trusted query caller/model permits identifier name or supplies suchorder; canonical generated reads expose no arbitrary client filter/order today, so remote SQL injection not shown.
findings.actual_consumer: Raw storage query/owner query internal caller; a hand-authored queryRecords order withconstructor field reaches toStorageOrder identifier forwarding.
findings.strongest_counterevidence: SQL values/model/IDs bound, unknown ordinary field names regex checked, direction constrained; prototype-safe projection and final mutation own-field check prevent corresponding object pollution. No external prototype pollution or arbitrary SQL execution claim.
findings.required_fix_acceptance: Use Map or own-property metadata lookup, then ordinary field validation; preserve accepted own identifier semantics. Source witness against both adapters and error envelope must remain safe.
findings.uncertainty: Low-scope current caller correctness/security hardening; no exploit or runtime outcome executed.
